papers.title: The Impact of Columnar and Equiaxed β-Grain Structures on Mechanical Anisotropy in High-Deposition-Rate Additively Manufactured α + β Titanium Alloys
papers.abstract: Abstract There is growing interest to produce α + β titanium alloys with high-deposition-rate additive manufacturing (DED-AM) processes for aerospace applications. However, there are still important aspects of their microstructure-mechanical property relationships that are not well understood, which are linked to the macro and microstructure heterogeneities generated by the AM processes and intrinsic titanium metallurgy that produce columnar β -grain structures. Trends in the literature, which are based primarily on Ti-6Al-4V data, have shown mechanical anisotropy is often present when samples exhibit coarse and columnar β -grain structures. This includes yield-stress and elongation anisotropy arising during uniaxial tensile testing, and crack growth rate anisotropy with high scatter recorded during fatigue testing, both of which are generally only tested in orientations parallel and perpendicular to the AM build direction. In this work, this mechanical anisotropy in α + β titanium alloys is investigated in more detail with Ti-6Al-4V and Ti-6Al-2Sn-4Zr-2Mo-0.1Si wire-arc additively manufactured test samples, comparing columnar parent β -grain structures to equiaxed grain structures. In particular, highlighting that the true yield-stress anisotropy in columnar grain samples is only revealed when testing the material at a 45 deg orientation away from the AM build direction. It is also shown that the large grain boundary α colonies that form on parent columnar β -grain boundaries have a significant impact on the fatigue crack growth rate data scatter. Refining the parent β -grain structures is demonstrated to resolve these issues and the related microstructure mechanisms were investigated in detail, using both experimental and crystal plasticity simulation methods. Finally, the formation and three dimensionality of the detrimental grain boundary α colonies that nucleate on columnar β -grain boundaries were investigated for the first time using in-situ SEM heating and 3D-EBSD techniques.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文直接研究增材制造Ti-6Al-4V的力学各向异性和疲劳行为，与用户关注的L1方向高度吻合。
llm.why_not_core: 该论文涉及Ti-6Al-4V和Ti-6Al-2Sn-4Zr-2Mo-0.1Si两种材料，但主要关注Ti-6Al-4V的力学各向异性，完全覆盖L1方向要求。

summary_zh.motivation: 探究高沉积速率增材制造α+β钛合金中柱状与等轴β晶粒结构对力学各向异性的影响。
summary_zh.method: 采用线弧增材制造Ti-6Al-4V和Ti-6Al-2Sn-4Zr-2Mo-0.1Si，结合拉伸、疲劳实验及晶体塑性模拟。
summary_zh.result: 柱状晶试样在45°方向显示出屈服应力各向异性，且大晶界α相增加疲劳裂纹扩展数据分散性。
summary_zh.validation: 通过实验测试和晶体塑性模拟验证微观结构对力学各向异性的影响。

summary_en.motivation: This work investigates the influence of columnar versus equiaxed β-grain structures on mechanical anisotropy in high-deposition-rate additively manufactured α+β titanium alloys, with particular focus on Ti-6Al-4V.
summary_en.method: Wire-arc additive manufacturing (DED) was used to produce Ti-6Al-4V and Ti-6Al-2Sn-4Zr-2Mo-0.1Si samples with columnar and equiaxed β-grains; tensile tests at 0°, 45°, and 90° orientations and fatigue crack growth tests were performed, supported by crystal plasticity simulations and in-situ SEM heating/3D-EBSD.
summary_en.result: Yield stress anisotropy in columnar-grained samples is only fully revealed when tested at 45° orientation, and large grain boundary α colonies on columnar β-grain boundaries significantly increase scatter in fatigue crack growth rates; refining β-grain structure alleviates these issues.
summary_en.validation: Experimental mechanical testing and crystal plasticity simulations validate the microstructure-driven anisotropy mechanisms.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文直接研究激光冲击强化和热处理两种后处理对Ti-6Al-4V合金摩擦学性能的影响，属于方向关注的后处理对力学性能的调控。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on tribological properties rather than fatigue or tensile strength, which are the primary mechanical performance metrics emphasized in the direction.

summary_zh.motivation: 提高激光粉末床熔融Ti-6Al-4V合金的耐磨性能。
summary_zh.method: 结合激光冲击强化与热处理对合金进行后处理。
summary_zh.result: 显著改善了合金的摩擦学性能。
summary_zh.validation: 通过摩擦磨损实验进行验证。

summary_en.motivation: To improve the wear resistance of laser powder bed fusion Ti-6Al-4V alloy through post-processing.
summary_en.method: Combining laser shock peening and heat treatment to modify the surface and bulk properties of the alloy.
summary_en.result: The combined post-processing significantly enhanced the tribological performance of the alloy.
summary_en.validation: Wear tests were conducted to evaluate the improvement in tribological properties.
